text.en: Akira, Sunita and Mary ran a 200 metre walking race. The winner took 1 minute 55 seconds, the second 1 minute 56 seconds and the third 1 minute 57 seconds. Minutes alone cannot tell us who won - we need a smaller unit: the second.

A race has small differences in time, so we use a new unit called the second.
The book tells us: 1 minute = 60 seconds. The second hand of a clock moves 60 steps in one full round, which takes exactly 1 minute.
And 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 1 hour = 60 x 60 = 3600 seconds.
Some things take seconds, like blinking, switching on a light or snapping fingers. Some take minutes, like filling a bucket or having a bath.
Estimate first and then check. In the book you estimate how many balloons you can blow, push-ups, breaths or hops on one leg in a minute, and then verify.
To read the time taken on a clock, look at the second hand. If Rani's second hand moved from 12 to 4, she took 20 seconds, because each number on the clock is 5 seconds.
When you draw the missing seconds hand: if Raghu took 20 seconds, the hand moves 4 numbers, to 4; 30 seconds is the 6; 60 seconds is a full round back to the same place.

problem.en: The second hand starts at 12 and stops at 8. How many seconds have passed?

text.en: From 12 to 8 the hand crosses 8 numbers.

why.en: Each number on the clock face is 5 seconds.
Multiply the number of numbers by 5.

prompt.en: How many seconds are there in 1 minute and how do you read seconds on a clock?

requiredIdeas.en: Each number on the clock face stands for 5 seconds
A full round of the second hand is 1 minute

commonMisconceptions.en: Reading the hour hand instead of the second hand

points.en: Seconds measure very short times like blinking or a race.
On a clock each number is 5 seconds for the second hand.
Estimate the time first, then check by doing.
